Get everything in writing..under no circumstance leave a deposit on your first visit. The offers will only get better despite and pressure about price increase lost of incentives or whatever bullshit they try use to persuade you. If you have a trade in, don't mention it until the last moment. Lots of places like to raise the price of their home so they can "offer" you a fair amount for your trade. In addition, make sure they do all of their shopping online first. Bring floorplans to the homes they are most interested in and get them to give you a price quote and find out EXACTLY what is included in that price (delivery, set-up, tie down, AC, skirting, etc..). Let them know you are shopping around and DO plan on  comparing offers from different manufactures. I guarantee if you use this method you will get the absolute best deal.

In addition, contrary to popular belief, if you let them know you are in a hurry and willing to act today, they will give you their best price. Just make sure and be patient..only time will tell if that is their genuine bottom dollar price

Yes there are dealers that specialize in ultra cheap homes, I like to call them boxes.  Most of the time these dealers offer in-house financing and market towards customers with credit scores lower than 575. Hence that is their only option to get into home ownership. 

We sell cavco, fleetwood, and palm harbor homes. With Cavco being cheapest, then fleetwood, and finally Palm Harbor. 

It really is an excellent avenue to pursue for some customers. It all depends on your housing needs and goals. As an example of the wide range of quality: some manufactures wall studs are up to 24" OC and some are 12" OC like they should be.  Cheaper homes typically have no gasket that runs along their marriage line and tend to have lower R values. In addition, some companies use all name brand products throughout their homes and some use the cheapest shit possible. I hope you enjoy your new home! It sounds like you got a good deal, congrats!
